title: Inline validation-error re-render discards the referee's submitted answer, unlike the /apply precedent it cites
evidence:
// Inline re-render (the /apply view_form_with_errors
              // precedent): the failed question current, the message inline.
              let draft = questions.decode_draft(row.draft_answers)
              render_form_page(
                token:,
                slot:,
                vars:,
                draft:,
                current_id: q.id,
                error_question: Some(q.id),
                error_message: message,
              )

form_handler.gleam:214:          prefill: questions.prefill_for(q:, draft:),

Precedent (application/application_handler.gleam:214):            _ ->
              form_pages.view_form_with_errors(
                vacancy,
                errors,
                values,
detail: A failed no-JS POST re-renders prefill only from the stored draft, so the invalid submission (e.g. 1000+ char free text, over-long other text) is wiped and must be retyped. The cited /apply precedent passes the submitted `values` into its re-render.
recommended_fix: Pass the submitted form values into render_form_page on the error branch and merge them over the draft prefill (fields present in the POST win), matching view_form_with_errors(values:) semantics.

title: month_year accepts an unpadded month ('2026-1'), storing a non-canonical value against the pinned YYYY-MM wire contract
detail: Only the year length is checked; '2026-1' splits to year_str '2026' and month_str '1', passes int.parse and the 1..12 range, and is stored verbatim. The draft contract pins YYYY-MM, which rc3-4's structurer consumes. Reachable only via tampered input.
recommended_fix: Require string.length(month_str) == 2 alongside the existing month range check so only the canonical zero-padded YYYY-MM wire format is stored.

title: thousands_separated/group_every_three re-implement the codebase's existing thousands-grouping helper
detail: The comma-grouping algorithm already exists as group_thousands (used by the public format_eur). The new module re-implements it on a String instead of reusing it; format_eur itself is not a drop-in because it prepends the € symbol the copy adds separately.
recommended_fix: Export group_thousands from content/layout.gleam (or add a symbol-free public wrapper) and call it from format_annual_salary instead of the private string-based copy.
